side_a: CC 3.4.5: `consent:partnership_grant` MUST be emitted by a `subject_key_id` of the target Contribution or a `delegates_to` chain rooted at one
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.3.1: **the partner** — the OTHER party (agent occurrence for `grant`, user identity for `accept`); singular, non-empty
note: The emitter gate of CC 3.4.5 wants the grant signed by a key in its own subject ids; the member table of CC 4.4.3.4.3.1 puts only the partner there, so the user who signs is never a subject and the gate refuses every grant. CC 4.4.3.5.3 ratified_pair is written to the second shape.

side_a: CC 3.3.5: subject_key_id: key_id // the subject declaring stance (federation_keys
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.3.1: subject_key_id: <the partner key: agent occurrence (grant) | user identity (accept)>
note: Same root as the row above: on the grant half `subject_key_id` is the declaring subject in CC 3.3.5 and the other party in CC 4.4.3.4.3.1. `ratified_pair` (CC 4.4.3.5.3) requires grant.subject_key_id == accept.attesting_key_id, which a row built to CC 3.3.5 never meets.

side_a: CC 3.3.7: Pinning `self` is what forecloses a third party forging a grant in G's name, since only G signs with G's key as the attested-intent-holder.
side_b: CC 6.1.5.3: is the `cohorts` member of the owner's `consent:replication` grant for that node
note: CC 3.3.7 admits a replication grant only from the granting node's own key; CC 6.1.5.3 and CC 3.3.6.3 (any live roster key signs every owner act, consent included) make it the owner's grant for the node. The family model (code-v61) and the CC 8.10 card admit both: `replication: owner, self`. A node built to CC 3.3.7 alone refuses the owner-signed grant that sets the per-node allow list.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: **Yes:** the ledger's single owner (the steward-bound identity of its `ledger_id` triple); no delegate writes
side_b: data manifests/namespace_registry.json: the ledger's single owner (the steward-bound identity of its ledger_id triple) or a delegate under its declared serialization discipline
note: The registry reserved_rule of ledger:head, ledger:checkpoint and ledger:promotion still admits a delegate; CC 3.1.3 and CC 3.3.10.1 clause 3 (a `delegates_to` edge confers no write on a ledger) refuse one. The family model notes "CC delegate arm: GAP". The text is the later and consistent side; the registry rule is stale.

side_a: CC 3.4.11: Admitted iff the signer acts for the subject (the subject's own occurrence or an admitted occurrence of it).
side_b: data manifests/namespace_registry.json: subject-or-steward-signed, not open-sender; no {level} token
note: Three answers to who may declare a person's age band: the text says the subject's own occurrences only; the registry gated-stem rule adds the steward; the family model cell (code-v61) and the transitions row say any registered key (`any_registered`, role `registered`). The band sets the protections applied to that person.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.4: Enable/disable is signed by the CC 4.5.5 `moderate`/`takedown` authority and revocable by `withdraws`
side_b: data manifests/namespace_registry.json: "prefix": "watchlist:{id}",
note: Text: only the moderate or takedown authority of a group turns a watchlist on for it. The registry row (next member `reserved: false`), the family model signer cell `any_registered` (code-v61), the transitions row and the CC 8.10 card (attest: `registered`) let any registered key attest one, and the reactions manifest then auto-fires the matcher. The registry row has `reserved: false` (the CC 3.1.9.4 table has no emitter column, as in C323).

side_a: CC 3.1.9.4: `petition` is the petitioner's own row that opens the ownership-reclaim ceremony
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: seat_role(wa) quorum, re-derived from this node's state
note: The model and transitions give one signer rule for every wa_adjudication state (role `wa`); under it the petitioner cannot file the petition leaf that CC 3.1.9.4 and CC 3.2 make the petitioner's own. The transitions row also gives the attest policy as `selfAct` (one voice) where the text says the other three states are quorum-emitted over the full seated roster.

side_a: CC 3.1.5: **A planned retirement is cancelled by the decider `withdraws`-ing the `decided` row**
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: none (held shut)
note: CC 3.1.5 and CC 7.5.5 reading (1) give two withdrawers of the `decided` row (the key named in `decided_by`, and the agent key) while no `frozen` row exists. The retirement:{state} lifecycle cell is "none (held shut)" and transitions.json has an attest transition only, so a system built from the data cannot cancel a planned retirement.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.2: **reserved — substrate-steward-emitted**, the emitter rule pinned at mint per R2(a), so the ProducerSteward default never applies.
side_b: data manifests/namespace_registry.json: "prefix": "regime:{artifact}:{version}",
note: The row calls the family reserved; the registry row has `reserved: false` and the model signer cell is `any_registered` with no cite. Same cause as C323 (the CC 3.1.9.2 table has no emitter column). Also the registry vocabulary for {artifact} holds `manifest` only where the row lists four.

side_a: CC 3.1.5.5: Emitted at `federation` scope by a key holding `infra:attest`, delegated by the root or conferred by an accord co-scrub of its key record
side_b: data manifests/namespace_registry.json: "prefix": "evidence:{suite}:{kind}:{cell}:{prefix}",
note: The text names the emitter (a key holding infra:attest); the model signer cell is `any_registered` (code-v61, reading "fills") and the registry has `reserved: false`. Whether the sentence is a gate or a description is not said; a reader weighs the row either way, so minor.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: the node's owner-binding chain — the owner, or the node it owns (self-or-owner, as [CC 3.4.5](part_3_the_namespace.md) reads `config:{scope}`)
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: owner_of_subject (binding in force at the signed instant)
note: Text admits two authors of consent:community_trust (the owner, or the owned node: "The node-authored form stays valid"). The leaf cell and the CC 8.10 card give `owner` only; the parent consent:{kind} cell carries the node-signed form as a note. A reader of the leaf cell alone refuses the node-authored grant.

side_a: CC 3.4.5: `consent:partnership_grant` MUST be emitted by a `subject_key_id` of the target Contribution or a `delegates_to` chain rooted at one
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: self | owner_of_subject(for_key_id) x none x {}; W on the owner's standing
note: For consent:state the text gives a subject or a delegation chain rooted at one (the CC 3.3.1 column gives the subject only); the consent:state cell (code-v61) has no delegation arm and adds the owner of the node named in for_key_id, which the CC 3.4.5 row does not list. consent:scope, stream and partnership_grant cells do carry the chain.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1: A substrate MUST refuse at admission a `key_grant` whose issuer neither owns or stewards the asset nor holds a `grant`-scoped delegation over it
side_b: CC 3.3.2: On the `epoch` axis the sealer is the minter, which MUST be an active member occurrence at `asserted_at`.
note: CC 2.4.1.2.1 states its refusal for every key_grant; on the epoch axis CC 3.3.2 and the CC 3.1.3 row admit any active member that mints, who owns or stewards nothing and holds no grant-scoped delegation. Read alone, CC 2.4.1.2.1 refuses a member-minted epoch grant. The data follows CC 3.3.2 (`minter | owner_of(content or stream)`).

side_a: CC 3.3.2: On the `content` and `stream` axes the sealer is a key that speaks for the blob's or stream's owner.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.1: For a `family` member the admitting host runs the walk after the member is admitted.
note: The re-key walk wraps every blob the cohort holds, other members' blobs included, and "writes the grant rows"; CC 4.4.3.4.1 does not say whose key signs them. Under the sealer rule the admitting host speaks for its own owner only, so its grant over another member's blob is refused. reactions.json has the walk emit key_grant:content "by identity:substrate_persist".

side_a: CC 6.1.9: A return is sent once per period by a node whose owner-binding chains to a bundle root
side_b: CC 3.1.3: **Yes — addressed:** the returning node's key; reach is the named seat only
note: CC 6.1.9 makes eligibility depend on the node's owner-binding chaining to a bundle root; the census:share row lists the door's refusals and none is for an ineligible sender, and the model cell is `self`. Whether an unowned or unrooted node's share is refused or only uncounted is not said.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.3: the conferrer of the seat, the person seated, or an agent that person handed the answering to
side_b: CC 4.3: An approval that authorises an identity amendment ([CC 3.1.5](part_3_the_namespace.md)) is not handed on: it is signed by the conferrer or by the person holding the unscoped seat.
note: The deferral:response row lists three attesters with no exception; CC 4.3 (the home, cited by the row) withholds one class of approval from the agent. A door built from the row admits an agent-signed approval of an identity amendment.

side_a: CC 4.5.9.1: or by a `delegates_to` chain with `scope: [consent_revocation]` — the substrate has no path to mint a location_proof on behalf of a key without an explicit signature
side_b: CC 4.5.9.3: - **Opt-in** (CC 4.5.9.1): the claim exists only because the subject signed and emitted it
note: CC 4.5.9.1 lets a holder of a `consent_revocation` delegation emit a location proof for the subject; CC 4.5.9.3 says only the subject's signature brings one into being, and CC 2.4.1.1 gives that scope to the rule-3 proxy for withdrawing only. Under the first a proxy (typically the agent holding the data) can state where a person is; under the second it cannot.

side_a: CC 3.4.6: `attesting_key_id` MUST be a current member of the community/stream the `{stream_id}` belongs to
side_b: CC 3.4.6: the role-set must contain a subscriber-eligible role (per the community's admission semantics
note: The emitter rule keys on membership alone; the composition paragraph adds a role-set condition and names no subscriber-eligible role. The model cell is `roster_member(at)` with no role condition, which follows the first.

side_a: CC 4.2.1: Humanity-accord authority signs nothing outside this enumeration.
side_b: CC 3.4.1: accord-holder self-attestation about the accord;
note: Known, still there and marked for Eric: the enumeration of CC 4.2.1 lists lifecycle rows but not `accord:human_dignity`; the model gives every accord:* family the signer `seat_role(holder)`. C051 is the same enumeration against the CC 4.2.6 roster-change objects.

side_a: CC 3.1.1: cosigned by the trust root for `steward_purge`
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: (takedown: outside vocabulary); steward_purge leaf: none (held shut)
note: Known (to fix in the data) and still there: transitions.json gives takedown_notice:{basis} one attest transition, role `takedown`, policy selfAct, for every basis; no cosigned policy for the steward_purge leaf.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: **Yes — the accord holders, cosigned at the charter's M**; never a single holder, never the node itself
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: holder quorum over the carried transport destination
note: The text and the family model signer and cosign cells make transport:canonical_rebind a quorum act. manifests/transitions.json and the CC 8.10 card (which CC 8.10 calls this document's statement of the value) give its attest transition role `holder`, policy `selfAct`: one voice. Under the card a single accord holder re-binds a seated serve node's transport. Same fault as C307 for the steward_purge leaf.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.2: Subject-scoped quarantine marker: **slash-duty-holder-only** emitter.
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: {attester, subject} (+ producer's owner, consent proxy rule 3, delegate rule 4: outside vocabulary)
note: The quarantine:{state} lifecycle cell (code-v61), the transitions row and the CC 8.10 card let the subject of a quarantine marker withdraw it (`withdraw: author, subject`). The text gives the marker plane to the slash-duty holder alone and CC 2.4.1.1 "admits no subject-side removal of an adverse row"; quarantine is not among the families the `adverse` departure reason moves. The same default lets the subject withdraw a wa_adjudication finding and a mesh_config row. Belongs to the withdraw key as well.

side_a: CC 3.2: Ownership MUST be resolved by `owner_of`, which reads owner-bindings and nothing else
side_b: CC 3.4.7.3: The `identity_occurrence` half yields **at most one** anchor, and the custody half yields **at most one**
note: Known and held (ask persist), still there: CC 3.2 and the definition in CC 3.4.7.3 read the steward from the one live owner-binding and nothing else; the Cardinality paragraph of CC 3.4.7.3 keeps a second, occurrence anchor, under which an agent may act through a node of a person who holds no owner-binding on it. C209 (`steward_of ==` in the fenced line) goes with it.

side_a: CC 3.2: a founding record seats a listed member iff that member signed it; no owner gate
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.2: That signature is admissible only from a key with a live federation-scope owner-binding
note: Joining a public room needs an announced owner because the room's rows are served to strangers; founding one is said to carry no owner gate. A founder whose binding is held at self only is seated by the first and could not have joined by the second. The reason given for the joiner applies to the founder as well.

side_a: CC 3.4.12: require  attester(capacity) ∉ {S, petitioner}
side_b: CC 3.1.2: the subject cannot self-emit it and the proposed steward cannot be the attester
note: The predicate and the rejection list of CC 3.4.12 bar the steward and the petitioner as assessor; the CC 3.1.2 catalogue row and the registry reserved rule ("attester != steward") bar the steward only. Same shortfall as C012 found in the review list. The family model marks even the steward test as a gap.

side_a: CC 3.4.12: **never plenary**, and time-boxed to the attestation's freshness window
side_b: CC 3.4.12: It is **rejected** when its `valid_until` outruns the review cadence
note: Two bounds on how long a substituted binding may run: the freshness window of the capacity attestation, and the review cadence (set by the community's policy and named in the row). The section does not say they are one period; where they differ the predicate enforces the cadence only.

side_a: CC 3.2: It is cosigned under that affiliation's protocol
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: affiliation named must admit the owner
note: For an agent held for an organisation the text requires the owner-binding to carry the affiliation's quorum; the ownership family's cosign cell is `none` (code-v61), its authorize transition is one voice (`selfAct`, role owner), and the placement cell reads the affiliation as only having to admit the owner. departure_reasons.json lists the cell as open. One steward's signature binds the organisation under the data and does not under the text.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: The substrate MUST refuse such a row whose `asserted_at` precedes the receiver's clock by more than `W`, with the refusal token **`asserted_at_stale`**.
side_b: CC 3.3.6.3: A row signed by a key that is still live admits at any age
note: Known, open and still there: CC 2.6.7 refuses every chain-judged row older than 72 h; CC 3.3.6.3 and CC 3.3.4 ("A signature by a member still standing counts at any age") apply W only to a signer that has lost standing at receipt. The model cells for consent:state, consent:replication, key_grant and ownership follow the second ("W on the owner's standing").

side_a: CC 2.6.7: a licence (`licensure:*`), a deferral response, the epoch-axis membership check — is judged at its signed `asserted_at`
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: receipt future-skew <=5 min, us resolution (check_instant_binding); no W; s3: signed instants .sssZ only (signed_instant_form_violation)
note: The freshness cells of licensure:{authority_id}, deferral:response:{outcome} and membership:{stage} are the default row: judged at receipt, no W (source generic). CC 2.6.7, CC 2.4.1.2.1 ("never at receipt") and CC 4.3 judge these rows at the signed instant and bound them by W. A licence issued before its authority's chain link was withdrawn stands under the text and is judged against today's chain under the cell. Bears on C117.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: Consumers receiving an attestation whose `asserted_at` is more than 5 minutes in the future MUST reject it as malformed.
side_b: CC 3.1.3.1: Peers MUST NOT re-apply any arrival-clock check to a replicated claim
note: Known (no conflict on reading): the session claim is the stated exception to the every-consumer future bound. Still worded so that its parenthesis reads as general. The session:{kind} freshness cell is the default "judged at receipt", which does not carry the exception.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: a pending row whose primary is no longer an active member at receipt is refused `asserted_at_stale` once its signed instant is older than the freshness window W
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json: not in the census
note: The cosign:{state} freshness cell is a gap (value null, "not in the census"), as are the two ballot families'. The CC 3.1.3 row and CC 3.3.4 state the rule in full: W on a signer no longer active, and no holding of an event signed more than one hold window before arrival.

side_a: CC 5.3.4: a root attaches by the pinned `bundle_fingerprint`, with `attach_window_secs` **604800**
side_b: CC 3.2: no head is fresh by cosignature, so none is attachable by cosignature
note: With witnessed mode off CC 3.2 T6 reads the attach gate as anchor-only and CC 2.1 defines attach_window_secs as the age of the newest counted witness cosignature, of which there is none. The 604 800 s default therefore gates nothing; a reader who applies it to the head's own age refuses an anchored root after seven days, against T4 (valid until revoked).

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.4.1: the resolving Consumer's own clock; membership is evaluated as of `now`
side_b: CC 3.1.3: the signer is an active member at the event's signed instant
note: Membership for a row's admission is read at the row's signed instant in CC 2.6.7, CC 3.1.3 and CC 3.3.2; CC 3.4.6 admits a delivery receipt from "a current member" resolved by Policy M, whose `now` is the reader's clock, and the ballot:moderator cell says "live at evaluation". A receipt signed by a member since removed is admitted at one node and refused at a later one. Policy M is a read-time resolution; CC 3.4.6 borrows it for admission.

side_a: CC 5.3.4: Unanimity is what that ceremony gathers, and any change to the charter or the roster takes it.
side_b: CC 5.3.4: Witnessed mode is turned on by an amendment signed by a strict majority of the standing accord roster.
note: Known and held, still there: one paragraph of CC 5.3.4 puts every charter or roster change at unanimity; the same section, CC 3.2 T4a/T6 and CC 4.2.6 put charter re-scrubs and roster changes at a strict majority. constants.tsv `charter_change_threshold` records the strict majority (settled_from C197), so the data now disagrees with the unanimity sentence.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.8: A charter MUST carry a pre-rotation commitment (the successor key committed in advance) and an m-of-n recovery ceremony
side_b: CC 2.6.1.2: member absent (no holder can self-rotate; recovery is a roster change)
note: CC 4.4.3.8 requires recovery commitments of every charter; CC 2.1, CC 2.6.1.2 and CC 2.6.1.7 require `recovery_commitments` on the accord's charter only and give a reading for its absence elsewhere. A root minted by another operator without commitments is non-conformant under the first and admitted under the second.

side_a: CC 1.13.2: Once `bootstrap_threshold ≥ 2`, no single Registry install can issue federation-scope attestations unilaterally.
side_b: CC 5.3.4: Nothing a serving install signs on its own account is a root.
note: `bootstrap_threshold` appears once in the document and is defined nowhere; the sentence implies that below 2 one install does issue federation-scope attestations alone. CC 5.3.4 and the CC 3.1.1 agent_files row ("human-held, never the installs'") give an install's own signature no authority at any threshold.

side_a: CC 7.5.8: the Wise Authority adjudicates only the federation's own deferrals.
side_b: CC 3.1.9.4: the other three are the quorum's finding, WA-quorum-emitted with the **denominator over the full seated roster, never the live subset**
note: CC 7.5.8 limits the Wise Authority to deferrals; CC 7.3.5 says deferrals and in-federation objections; CC 3.2 and CC 3.1.9.4 also have a WA quorum find abandonment, seizure and succession of a key's ownership, and CC 7.5.5 has a WA approve release of a sealed archive. The narrow sentences are about legal claims and are shorter than the set of things a WA rules on.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: there is no steward cap on who relays
side_b: CC 5.4.6: **Who is a relay for a period:** a node
note: Known (proposed, not applied): item 4 of the anonymous tier defines the relay set for a period from nodes owner-bound under a root in the genesis charter set, while the default-behaviour text speaks of every announced node relaying with no cap. Still as it was.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.8: While set it **overrides both** the retention schedule **and** consent-driven descent, pinning named records above the noise floor.
side_b: CC 4.5.3: These bases terminate descent at zero, overriding the [CC 6.1.2.2](part_6_the_coherence_mathematics.md) retained floor
note: Known and marked for Eric, still there: a record under a legal hold that is also hit by an immediate-removal basis or a root's purge is pinned by one sentence and destroyed by the other; neither names the other.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.2.8: bind an affiliation and bind no community, save a community that issues a legal-weight licence class
side_b: CC 7.5.5: A `legal_hold` set, lifted, or violated on a retirement record is a `hard_case` of the kinds registered at [CC 3.1.9.4](part_3_the_namespace.md).
note: CC 4.4.3.2.8 makes the legal hold a limb of an affiliation's record and of nothing else; CC 7.5.5 and the CC 3.1.5 preserve_request row ("active `legal_hold` ids") put holds on the retirement record of any agent, whose steward may be a person with no affiliation. Who may set a hold on such a record is not said. No family carries the hold itself: the manifests name it only inside hard_case kinds.

side_a: CC 4.5.1: Only privileges require justification, and only privileges belong on this register.
side_b: CC 1.13.2: The maker's power over the made is listed on the [CC 4.5.1](part_4_composition_governance.md) register for visibility, with its bounds, as the condition of symmetry and not as an asymmetry.
note: The register is said to hold privileges only, and one of its rows is expressly not a privilege and not an asymmetry: the maker's power, the halt included, listed for visibility as the condition of symmetry. CC 4.5.1 explains the listing in its own text, so a careful reader resolves it; the "only privileges" sentence in CC 1 and CC 4.5.1 is the short side.
